BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilg.gov.ph OILG OPINION NO S. 08 HON. BENJAMIN B. MAGALONG City Mayor Baguio Dear Mayor Magalong: We are in receipt of a Memorandum dated December 14, 2023, from Regional Director Araceli A. San Jose, DILG-CAR, relative to your letter dated November 28, 2023, seeking clarification on the entitlement of honorarium to barangay officials who have not been re-elected but have attended and completed two (2) regular barangay meetings in the month preceding the end of their term. At the outset, may we note that we are not furnished with a copy of your letter. Nevertheless, as represented in the said Memorandum, the concerned barangay officials attended regular barangay meetings in November 2023. However, it appears that the City Accountant withheld their honorarium out of apprehension that they may not be entitled to it in light of the advisory from COMELEC stating that the only requirements for a newly-elected barangay official to assume office are proclamation and taking the requisite oath of office. This Department is of the view that Sangguniang Barangay meetings or sessions that were actually attended by the concerned outgoing barangay officials during the period that the newly-elected barangay officials have not yet assumed office are subject to the payment of honorarium. Our view is anchored to the pronouncement of the Supreme Court in Macalintal v. COMELEC, et al. 1, pertinent portion of which reads: "[W]hile the Court hereby declares RA 11935 unconstitutional, it recognizes the legal practicality of proceeding with the holding of the BSKE on the last Monday of October 2023, as provided under RA 11935. Additionally, the sitting BSK officials shall continue to hold office until their successors shall have been elected and qualified. But, their term of office shall be deemed to have ended on December 31, 2022, consistent with the provisions of RA 116462, that is, "on the first Monday of December 2025 and every three years (3) thereafter." Finally, the Congress is not precluded by these pronouncements from further amending the provisions of RA 9164, but the same shall be subject to the proper observance of the guidelines provided in the succeeding discussions." (Emphasize supplied) 1 G.R. NO. 263590, June 27, 2023 "Matino, Mahusay, at Maaasahan" Trunkline: (02) 8876-3454

In relation thereto, in Uy v. COMELEC2, the Supreme Court made the following discussions on assumption to office, thus: "xxx The theory on "assumption of office" which coincides on June 30 following the election is an over-stretched interpretation of the constitutional provision. The language of the provision is about the commencement of the term of office of "members" which shall begin "at noon on the thirtieth day of June next following their elections." This provision likewise sets the rule on term limitation such that "[n]o member of the House of Representatives shall serve for more than three consecutive terms." However, the term of office refers to a fixed duration which is not analogous to assumption of office that pertains to overt acts in the discharge of one's duties. Also, the term of office cannot be constructive but must involve actual discharge of duties xxx." Parenthetically, Item 3.3 of DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2023-1663, provides: "3. Outgoing Barangay and SK Officials 3.1 xxx 3.2. xxx 3.3 When necessary and when the newly elected officials of the barangay have not yet completely assumed office, ensure payment of recurring legitimate obligations of the barangay, particularly utility bills, salaries and honorarium only (barangay officials/employees) only." Thus, where these barangay sessions were actually attended by incumbent barangay officials pending the taking of oath and assumption to office of the newly-elected barangay officials, the incumbent barangay officials should be paid their honorarium pertaining to the sessions they actually attended. Thus, where these barangay sessions were actually attended by outgoing barangay officials—pending the taking of oaths and assumption of office of the newly-elected barangay officials—they should be paid their honorarium accordingly. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, B Authority of the Secr tary: ATTY. VI TOR R. LLAMAS U ecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUS LA/JVULLLS/LRALLD/jam cc: DIR. ARACELI A.
